title: Maximize Greatness of an Array
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, you can rearrange it into a new array perm.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, you can rearrange it into a new array perm. The greatness of nums is the count of indices where perm[i] is greater than nums[i]. Determine the highest possible greatness by permuting nums.
constraints: Permute nums into a new array using every occurrence exactly once.
Greatness counts positions where the permuted value is strictly greater than the original value.
hints: Sort both the source targets and candidate permuted values.
Scan candidates from smallest upward and match a candidate only when it strictly exceeds the smallest unmatched target.
Advance the target pointer on each successful match.
Using the smallest possible winning candidate preserves all larger candidates, so the greedy matching has maximum cardinality.
editorial: Using the smallest possible winning candidate preserves all larger candidates, so the greedy matching has maximum cardinality.

tests.explanation: Four larger values can be matched to four smaller original positions.
Values two, three, and four beat one, two, and three respectively, giving greatness three.
